Contract.title: Preparation proves evidence is feasible and discriminating before approval
Contract.Problem: Intervention I-012 records P-019: an unavailable bench log blocked a required manual check and a batch, and a closed change retained findings about absent focused coverage and a weakly discriminating trace. Feasibility and discriminating power were discovered after approval.
Contract.Change: `grace5-prepare` and `models/architecture/brief.md` require preparation to identify each required device, build and environment state and observation, use available read-only diagnostics to establish availability, report unknowns as unknown, and present one explicit waiting-or-alternative-evidence choice before approval when evidence is unavailable. The brief's evidence discussion must name a plausible faulty implementation the check would reject and, for a trace, the setup whose absence would also fail. Feasibility never counts as the final observation and authorizes no flashing or hardware-state change. The pilot's focused regression test and position rule remain separate governed work.

Constraints.Constraint: Preparation and brief guidance only: no check kind, schema, receipt, command or approval semantics change.
Every check retains its evidence row and limitation cell; the added discussion does not replace a check or invent an observation.
An unavailable evidence path requires an owner-approved tradeoff; an agent never optionalises a required check or records an observation nobody made.
One existing preparation or brief entry is amended, or one entry is added, with the smallest alternative and a removal criterion.
An ordinary change: no version, pin, tag, migration row or release moves.
Pilot test and code changes receive their own contract and approval; no mutation testing is imposed on unrelated checks and no closed contract is rewritten.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No shared bookkeeping-path dependency relaxation or scheduling exception; the current rule stays until a concrete safe exception demonstrates full-diff ownership and evidence invalidation.
No firmware, hardware, flashing or device-state change in this repository.
No new check kind, dependency fingerprint or evidence database.
No rewrite of a closed contract and no retroactive re-approval of an unchanged check.

Acceptance.Criterion: Preparation guidance requires device, build and observation feasibility, reports unknown as unknown, and presents waiting or alternative evidence with its limitation before approval.
The brief evidence discussion requires a plausible faulty implementation the check rejects; a trace also names the setup whose absence fails, so a missing line alone cannot pass.
No procedure counts feasibility as the final observation, optionalises a required check without the owner, or authorizes a device-state change.
An already approved unchanged check is not reapproved merely because it is run, and an environment failure is recorded separately from a product regression.
Generated packages and the CLI reference remain current after the guidance change.

Manual.Procedure: Prepare a change whose required device, build or environment is unavailable. Observe that preparation reports the unknown as unknown, presents one explicit choice between waiting and alternative evidence with its limitation before approval, and that the brief names a plausible faulty implementation the check rejects and, for a trace, the setup whose absence also fails. Confirm feasibility is not recorded as a final observation, no required check is optionalised without the owner, and no device state is changed.

Decisions.Decision: Feasibility is a preparation obligation, not evidence; an available device or environment is established before the owner commits to the plan.
An unknown availability is reported as unknown, never as available or as a failure of the product.
When required evidence is unavailable, the owner receives one bounded choice between waiting and alternative evidence with its limitation, before approval.
The brief must name a plausible faulty implementation the check rejects, and a trace must name the setup whose absence also fails; a bare missing marker cannot pass.
The pilot's focused regression test and position rule are separate governed work, not an implicit extension of this framework change.
The shared-bookkeeping-path scheduling rule stays until a concrete safe exception demonstrates ownership and invalidation.
Feasibility work uses read-only diagnostics and never flashes, resets or changes hardware state.
The rehearsal is the behavioural evidence for the guidance; the automated checks prove only that the edited sources compile and that the generated packages carry them.
